chatbot_text.name: Chatbot or template text
chatbot_text.explain: Contains a phrase only a chatbot or an unfilled template produces, such as “I'm unable to generate a review” or “[Hotel Name]”.

copied_text.name: Copied text

voice_mismatch.name: Not in the reviewer's own voice
voice_mismatch.explain: The reviewer's other reviews are written very differently. An AI model compared them and quotes the difference; both are shown side by side. Typical of scripted or incentivised reviews posted from real accounts.

keyword_style.name: Written like a search ad
keyword_style.explain: Names the business or its category together with its neighbourhood or city, the way search ads are written (“packers and movers in [area], [city]”), as several accounts here do.

first_time_burst.name: First-time accounts in a burst
first_time_burst.explain: Posted in a sudden burst of reviews that came mostly from accounts that have reviewed nothing else.

linked_group.name: Linked reviewer group
linked_group.explain: The reviewer belongs to a group of accounts that reviewed the same unrelated businesses in distant cities.

ai_style.name: Reads as AI-written
ai_style.explain: An AI model thinks this reads as written by a chatbot, and quotes the phrases why. That's an opinion, not proof: real customers also polish honest reviews with AI.

review_spree.name: Reviewing spree
review_spree.explain: The reviewer rated many unrelated businesses in several cities within a month, nearly all 5★: the shape of “rate and earn” tasks, though some travellers review this way too.

first_time_account.name: First-time account
first_time_account.explain: The account shows no other reviews. Many real customers create an account just to leave one review, so this alone isn't a warning sign.

evidence.text: 12 accounts that reviewed this business also reviewed the same 6 other businesses in 4 different cities, mostly within the same week.
15 of the latest 82 reviews arrived within 4 days (normally about 4 a week); 13 of them are 5★. Consistent with an in-store review drive or a campaign.
The 2 randomly chosen reviewers shared no other places with this group.

caveats: This is a pattern, not proof.
Only the newest 82 reviews and the 29 highest-priority reviewers were examined.
Dates in reviewer histories are approximate.
Rings within a single city aren't detected.
Google may already have removed some reviews.
A business can be targeted without its knowledge: review-task scams hand recruits real businesses to review.
